body.statement: Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\), under independent multinomial sampling and \(n/n_m\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\) when margins are estimated, the deterministic selector \(\widehat\chi_n\) chooses an incident first-order-compatible rigid chart and \(\widehat\gamma_n=1\) with probability tending to one. On these certified separated rigid charts, \(\widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_{\zeta}\), \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)\Rightarrow N(0,V_{\tau})\), and \(\widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}V_{\tau}\). Because \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\), scalar contrasts and the elliptical branch of \(W_n\) have asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\). If no chart is certified, the total procedure returns \(\widehat\chi_n=\bot\), \(\widehat\tau_n=(0,0)\), \(\widehat V_n=I_2\), and \(W_n=[0,1]^2\), with no covariance-consistency or Wald-coverage assertion for that fallback branch.
body.justification: The chart rule, covariance formula, and nonsingularity margin make regular-stratum Wald inference operational and falsifiable.
body.gap: The anchor and earlier response-type estimators establish regular-case normality only for their inverse formulas, not for deterministically selected rational and simple algebraic rigid charts.
body.consumer: Separated empirical tables obtain reproducible standard errors and Wald regions on every first-order-compatible atlas chart.

obligation.what_is_open: Unconditional correctness of the deterministic chart selector for the claimed atlas on every separated rigid stratum.
obligation.obstruction: The multinomial delta-method and Wald calculations close after local chart exhaustiveness is known. Until mixed-support exhaustion is proved, an omitted incident or nearby incompatible component can invalidate the selector claim.
obligation.attempted: Completed the chart-distance, slack-continuity, common-Jacobian Taylor expansion, sandwich consistency, positive-definiteness, Wald-coverage, and fallback calculations conditional on local exhaustiveness.
obligation.partial_result:
Conditional on local exhaustiveness of the finite certified atlas, independent multinomial sampling and proportional independent margin sampling give
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)\Rightarrow N(0,\Omega_{\zeta}),
\qquad
\widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_{\zeta}.
\]
For an incident chart \(\chi\), the definition of distance to its closed domain and the fact that \(\zeta\) belongs to that closure imply
\[
d_{\chi}(\widehat\zeta_n)
\le \|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2
=O_P(n^{-1/2})
=o_P(t_n),
\qquad t_n=n^{-1/4}.
\]
Continuity of \(\eta_{\chi}\) and \(\eta_{\chi}(\zeta)\ge\varepsilon\) make the slack test pass with probability tending to one, while distance at least \(\varepsilon\) from each incompatible chart closure makes every incompatible distance test fail with probability tending to one.  The common value and Jacobian on incident charts and their twice continuously differentiable extensions give
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)
=J_{\chi}(\zeta)\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)+o_P(1).
\]
Thus the continuous mapping theorem yields the stated Gaussian limit, and continuity of the sandwich map yields \(\widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}V_{\tau}\).  The lower eigenvalue bound \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\) implies eventual positive definiteness and ordinary Wald coverage.  The fallback identities follow directly from the definitions.  This closes the asymptotic calculation once the incident chart family is locally exhaustive; that last premise is not yet available from the unresolved global atlas theorem.
